Databricks implementation field guide

Healthcare Insights Platform

MedCare Regional Health Network

I use this page to learn and revise how I built a governed data platform. It pulls clinical data from Amazon S3 and patient, support, appointment and billing data from Salesforce. It ends in a dashboard and a plain-language Q&A layer.

  • Architecture

⚠This is a learning specificationImportant

This is not a clinically validated system. The data is synthetic and the build ran in a learning environment.

One rule matters more than any other. Patient-specific retrieval must enforce authorization at retrieval time. A prompt that says "only show this patient's data" is not access control. I do not treat patient-level search as safe unless the filter comes from a verified identity, outside the model. I flag where my own build falls short of that in the accuracy notes.

01The problem I am solving

Spec · Scenario Notes · §1–2

MedCare Regional Health Network keeps raw clinical data in an Amazon S3 bucket. It keeps patient and billing data in Salesforce. I need to bring both into Databricks and do four things:

  1. Refine the data into trusted metrics.
  2. Let patients ask about their own records in plain language.
  3. Give administrators a dashboard of activity across departments.
  4. Keep every step secured and governed.

This is not "load some CSVs and make some charts". The real chain is longer:

The final platform is not one application. It is one shared, governed data foundation with several ways to consume it.

The four outcomes I am building#

1 · Trusted healthcare data

I bring all eight datasets into Databricks. I keep the original data in Bronze, clean and connect it in Silver, and build purpose-made Gold tables.

2 · Healthcare analytics

Gold holds the metrics: readmission rate, length of stay, abnormal lab rate, appointment no-show rate, claim turnaround and approval rate, department visits and patient Q&A adoption.

3 · Natural-language Q&A

Gold data plus Case descriptions feed AI Search and an LLM. The system answers patient questions and administrator questions. Patient answers may only expose that patient's data.

4 · Secure operational dashboard

Administrators get views filterable by facility and date range: visits, patient questions, readmissions, no-shows, claims and abnormal labs.

02Source data I need

Spec · Data Sources Notes · §3

Eight datasets feed the platform. S3 and Salesforce are complementary, not competing. Clinical and operational data mostly comes from S3. Patient, support, appointment and billing data comes from Salesforce.

File / Object System What it holds
lab_results.csv Amazon S3 One row per lab test: patient MRN, department, test name/code, result value, reference range, abnormal flag, collection and result timestamps.
patient_vitals.csv Amazon S3 Device-recorded vitals (heart rate, SpO2, blood pressure, temperature), tied to patient MRN, department and ward.
hospital_admissions.csv Amazon S3 Admission and discharge records: department, diagnosis code, attending provider, discharge disposition, readmission flag.
patient_queries.csv Amazon S3 Log of questions patients submit through the portal or app: channel, category, timestamp, raw question text.
Account (Patient) Salesforce Patient master record: demographics, contact info, primary care provider.
Case Salesforce Patient complaints and support cases: case type, priority, status, resolution date.
Appointment__c Salesforce Scheduled visits: appointment date, clinic, department, provider, status (Completed / No-show / Cancelled).
Claim__c Salesforce Billing claims: claim amount, payer, submitted date, approved date, status.
Nothing matches that filter.
ℹWhat I will not assume

The spec does not define these. I treat them as design decisions I make later, not as facts:

  • exact row counts and historical date range
  • the exact Salesforce environment and field API names
  • the facility list, department lookup contents and diagnosis lookup values
  • the exact LLM model and patient authentication mechanism
  • dashboard implementation details
  • the S3 ingestion mechanism and any incremental/CDC mechanism
  • how synthetic data gets loaded into Salesforce

03Architecture at a glance

Spec · Bronze → Gold Notes · §4, §11, §15

Data moves in one direction: source, Bronze, Silver, Gold. Gold then feeds two consumers. Unity Catalog governance wraps every layer.

Each layer has one job#

Layer Question it answers What it does
Bronze "What exactly did I receive?" Stores source data as-is, plus metadata.
Silver "Can I trust and use this data?" Standardizes, validates, deduplicates, joins, calculates, quarantines.
Gold "Can the business use these metrics directly?" Curated tables for reporting, search and Q&A.
AI Search "Can I retrieve the relevant information?" Finds relevant rows or text.
UC functions "Can I calculate trusted metrics?" Runs fixed, governed analytics.
LLM / agent "Can I understand the question and pick the right tool?" Reads the question, calls tools, writes the answer.

04Bronze: preserve the source

Spec · Bronze Layer Build · Steps 1–2 Revision · §1

The spec rule is short. Load all four CSV files and all four Salesforce objects as-is. Add source_system, file_name (or object_name) and load_timestamp to every row. Do no cleaning and no joins.

What I built#

  1. I generated the project data, created the S3 source and created the Salesforce records.
  2. I connected S3 to Databricks. The chain is Databricks → Unity Catalog → AWS IAM → S3.
  3. I connected Salesforce.
  4. I ingested the four CSVs with Auto Loader. One triggered, serverless pipeline run handled the existing files.
  5. I ingested the four Salesforce objects with Lakeflow Connect.
  6. I added the required metadata columns to the Salesforce Bronze tables.

The S3 pipeline created four streaming tables. These are the row counts shown in the pipeline run:

Bronze table Rows loaded
lab_results 15,075
patient_queries 6,060
patient_vitals 30,120
hospital_admissions 4,200

The file-reading pattern#

For file-based data I think of read_files as: "read the CSV files from S3 and give me a table-like result". I do no heavy cleaning here.

Why Salesforce Bronze is different#

Salesforce connector tables can receive updates. My S3 files are append-style. Databricks warns that a streaming read errors when the source has change commits, while materialized views reflect the current source data. So the Salesforce Bronze objects are materialized views over the connector tables. They take load_timestamp from SystemModstamp.

ℹSchema names are not consistent in my notes

The S3 Bronze tables appear as healthcare_insights.project_bronze in Step 2 and in the Silver code. The security step and the recap call the Bronze schema medcare_bronze. The Salesforce connector lands in healthcare_insights.bronze. I am not sure whether project_bronze was renamed. I need to confirm this in the workspace.

05Data model and keys

Spec · Silver Layer Notes · §5, §12

patient_mrn is the central integration key. The spec says to keep it as the join key to clinical data. It is also how I connect Salesforce patient data to clinical records.

Two joins are named explicitly. Vitals join to admissions on patient_mrn + facility_id to attach admission context. A claim links to an admission through admission_id where applicable.

Relationship Status Why I label it that way
Account → labs, vitals, admissions on patient_mrn Specified The spec says to keep patient_mrn as the join key to clinical data.
Account → Case on patient_mrn Specified Silver rule: "link each case to patient_mrn".
Vitals → admissions on patient_mrn + facility_id Specified Named in the vitals Silver rule. My build also checks that the reading falls inside the admission period.
Claim → admission on admission_id Specified "link to admission_id where applicable".
Account → Appointment and Claim on patient_mrn Assumed The spec links appointments to department and provider, and claims to admission. It names no patient key for them. My patient_360 needs one, so I assumed it.
Account → patient query on patient_mrn Assumed The spec's column list for the query log has no MRN. My Silver code partitions queries by patient_mrn, so the column exists in my data.
department and facility_id as shared keys Assumed Implied by row filters and dashboard filters. The spec defines no department or facility table.
★Why keys come first

If the relationships are wrong, patient_360, the metrics, the dashboard numbers and the Q&A answers can all go wrong at once. So I treat identity and key standardization as foundational.

Six hidden dependencies I noticed#

The spec does not list these as a table. They are implied by the requirements.

06Silver: make the data trustworthy

Spec · Silver Layer Build · Step 3 Revision · §2–§20

The spec says: clean, standardize and connect each Bronze table so records can be trusted and joined across sources. In practice Silver does these jobs:

  • standardize identifiers, values and units
  • validate dates
  • remove duplicates
  • handle missing data
  • connect datasets and calculate derived fields
  • quarantine bad records
  • link Salesforce data to clinical data

I built Silver as materialized views. The SQL pattern is CREATE OR REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW … AS SELECT …. Pick a table below to see the spec rule and what I built.

Spec: standardize patient_mrn format, convert result values to consistent units, validate reference ranges, drop duplicate lab_result_id, flag and quarantine rows with missing collected_datetime.

What I built:

  • Rows with a missing collected_datetime go to lab_results_quarantine.
  • Valid rows stay in Silver lab_results.
  • I standardize patient_mrn and unit names, and keep numeric values.
  • I extract reference_min and reference_max from the reference range.
  • I recalculate abnormal_flag from the range when I can.
  • I remove duplicate lab_result_id values.

Deduplication with ROW_NUMBER(). For each lab_result_id, I number records from newest to oldest. WHERE rn = 1 keeps the newest.

lab_result_id result_datetime rn kept?
LAB001 10:30 1 yes
LAB001 10:20 2 no
LAB001 10:10 3 no
LAB002 11:00 1 yes

Range check. result_value BETWEEN reference_min AND reference_max means reference_min <= result_value <= reference_max. With a range of 10–20, a result of 15 is inside and 25 is outside. This gives the abnormality flag.

Spec: standardize vital_type naming (for example bp_systolic vs blood_pressure_systolic), remove sensor duplicate readings within the same minute, join to admissions on patient_mrn + facility_id to attach admission context.

What I built:

  • I standardize vital_type.
  • I use DATE_TRUNC('MINUTE', reading_datetime) so readings at 10:15:03, 10:15:27 and 10:15:51 all become 10:15:00. Then ROW_NUMBER() can find several readings in the same minute.
  • I attach admission context with a LEFT JOIN. I keep every vital reading, even when no admission matches.

The join is deliberately stricter than patient alone:

Same patient, same facility, and the vital happened during the admission. That is much safer than joining on the patient only.

Spec: validate that discharge_datetime is after admission_datetime, calculate length_of_stay, standardize diagnosis_desc against a lookup table, compute readmission_flag with a 30-day lookback if it is not already set.

What I built:

  • Rows where discharge is earlier than admission are marked invalid and left out of the clean output.
  • Length of stay is in hours: UNIX_TIMESTAMP difference divided by 3600, rounded to 2 decimals.
  • A blank or missing diagnosis_desc becomes Unknown.
  • I calculate the 30-day readmission flag.
⚠Known gap: the diagnosis lookup tableImportant

The spec asks me to standardize diagnosis_desc against a lookup table. I did not finish that. Blank diagnoses became Unknown, and the external lookup was not built.

Spec: classify query_category consistently, strip PII from free-text query_text before indexing, deduplicate resubmitted queries, standardize channel values.

What I built:

  • I map category variants to standard values with CASE. The mapping I looked at has Appointment, Billing, Lab Results, Medication and General.
  • I use REGEXP_REPLACE to replace email, phone, MRN and date-of-birth patterns with tags such as [EMAIL REDACTED].
  • I partition by patient_mrn, channel, query_category and query_text, order by query_timestamp DESC, and keep the latest row. That removes resubmissions.
＋Added note · what the redaction does not coverAdded

The patterns cover email, phone, MRN and date of birth. They do not cover names or other free-text details. Regex redaction is a first filter, not full de-identification. I should review a sample of the redacted text before I index it.

Spec: mask or tokenize name, phone, email and address. Keep patient_mrn as the join key. Deduplicate patient records across facilities.

What I built:

  • Standardize patient_mrn.
  • Hash and mask the PHI columns. MD5() turns the name into a hash. I keep the first 10 characters and add a prefix, for example 'PATIENT_' || SUBSTRING(MD5(Name), 1, 10). Phone follows the same idea with a PHONE_ prefix.
  • Deduplicate by patient_mrn and keep the latest SystemModstamp.

MD5 is hashing, not encryption. I cannot turn the hash back into the name. For this project it gives a consistent pseudonymous ID while hiding the real value.

＋Added note · MD5 is weak for this jobAdded

This is my own caution, not from the spec. An unsalted MD5 of a short, guessable value such as a name can be matched by trying likely names. For a real system I would use a keyed or salted method, or a token vault. For this demo it is fine.

Spec: standardize case_type and status, link each case to patient_mrn, calculate resolution_time_hours.

What I built: Silver case has patient_mrn, facility_id, department, case_type, case_status and resolution_time_hours.

Resolution time is the difference in seconds divided by 3600. A case created at 10:00 and resolved at 14:30 gives 4.5 hours. A CASE expression stops me from calculating a time for an unresolved case.

Spec: standardize status values (Completed / No-show / Cancelled / Rescheduled), link to department and provider, calculate lead_time_days between booking and appointment.

What I built: appointment_status, the retained department, provider_id and lead_time_days.

DATEDIFF(appointment_date, booking_date) gives the lead time. Booked Jan 1 and appointment Jan 10 means 9 days.

Spec: standardize claim status, calculate turnaround_days between submitted_date and approved_date, link to admission_id where applicable.

What I built: claim_status, turnaround_days, the retained admission_id where applicable, and the payer information Gold needs.

DATEDIFF(approved_date, submitted_date) gives the turnaround. Submitted Jan 1 and approved Jan 6 means 5 days. For Pending, Denied or Rejected claims there is no approval date, so turnaround_days stays NULL. That is correct, because there is no completed approval to measure.

08Gold: the consumption layer

Spec · Gold Layer Build · Step 4 Notes · §6, §24–25

Gold is not one table. It is a set of curated tables for reporting, search and Q&A. The dashboard should read Gold. It should not rebuild healthcare metrics from raw or Silver data.

Gold table Grain / dimensions Metrics produced
patient_360 One row per patient Demographics, latest vitals, latest lab results, current admission status, open cases. Answers patient-specific questions.
readmission_metrics Department, facility, diagnosis category, month 30-day readmission rate
length_of_stay_metrics Department, facility Average and median length of stay
lab_result_metrics Facility, department, test type, week Total results, abnormal results, abnormal %; trended weekly
appointment_metrics Department (with facility and date) No-show rate, cancellation rate, average lead time
claims_metrics Facility, payer, month Total claims, average turnaround days, approved claims, approval rate %
department_visit_metrics Department, with period_type (day / week / month / year) Visits = admissions + appointments
patient_query_metrics Category, channel, week / month / year Count of patient questions, for adoption tracking
Nothing matches that filter.

Patterns I used in Gold#

NULLIF(denominator, 0) stops a divide-by-zero error. The status literal in this snippet is the conceptual example from my revision notes.

  • Length of stay: AVG() gives the average. PERCENTILE_APPROX(..., 0.5) gives the median without sorting the whole dataset exactly, so it is an approximation. WHERE length_of_stay_hours IS NOT NULL keeps missing values out.
  • Readmission: I included DATE_TRUNC('MONTH', admission_datetime) AS metric_month. The dashboard needs a date-range filter and a monthly trend by department.
  • Lab metrics: I use CAST(abnormal_flag AS STRING) before checking it. That keeps the calculation safe whether Silver stores a Boolean or a string.
  • Department visits: one table with period_type. The dashboard switches between daily, weekly, monthly and yearly views instead of using four tables.
★Grain is part of the metric

A metric is not only a number. It also has a level: day, week, month or year. I must never add day rows, week rows, month rows and year rows together. That double-counts the same events. For "this week" I use week data. For "this month" I use month data.

★Admissions are not unique patients

admission_count is not the number of patients. One patient can have 3 admissions and 5 appointments and still be 1 unique patient. If a dataset has no distinct-patient metric, I say "unique patient count is not available". I never add admissions and appointments to make one.

patient_360 in detail#

patient_360 has exactly one row per patient. I first reduce each one-to-many source (vitals, labs, cases) to its latest or current information. Then I join the results.

It held 1,001 rows. One row had a null MRN, so 1,000 rows were identifiable patients.

The department bug I fixed. My first version used COALESCE(ca.department, 'Unknown') AS department. But ca comes from current_admission, which only holds admissions that are active right now. Discharged patients had no row there, so their department became Unknown. The whole table ended up as Unknown.

After the fix, patient_360 counts by department were:

Department Patients
Cardiology 133
Oncology 128
Pediatrics 126
General Medicine 124
Neurology 123
Emergency 122
Nephrology 121
Orthopedics 107
Unknown 17

Gold metric rows also describe events or periods. They are not unique patients. That became important when I tested the AI agent.

09Security and governance

Spec · Security & Governance Build · Steps 5–13 Notes · §9–10, security recap

Security is not an add-on. The spec calls this "the actual access model, not just general controls". It has to shape the data model, the department and patient keys, the Gold design and the Q&A path from the start. I did it before exposing the dashboard or the AI layer.

The six roles#

Pick a role to see what it can and cannot reach.

Can access
Gold + Silver data for their own department only; full patient_360 for their patients
Cannot access
PHI or records from other departments
How
Row-level security policy filtering on department; Unity Catalog row filter function
Can access
Gold metrics for their own department (readmission, no-show, LOS); no raw PHI
Cannot access
Any Silver or Bronze table; other departments' data
How
Grant SELECT on Gold views only, scoped by row filter on department
Can access
Claim__c, claims_metrics, patient_mrn as join key
Cannot access
Lab results, vitals, clinical notes
How
Column masking hides clinical columns; grant limited to the billing schema
Can access
All Gold metrics, all departments, no PHI columns
Cannot access
Bronze and Silver tables; masked PHI columns
How
Grant SELECT on Gold schema only; column mask applied account-wide
Can access
Bronze, Silver, Gold: full schema for pipeline build and debug
Cannot access
Nothing restricted, but access is logged and time-boxed
How
Elevated grant tied to a project group, reviewed periodically
Can access
Only their own patient_360 record, matched to their logged-in identity
Cannot access
Any other patient's data; department-level aggregates
How
Query-time filter on patient_mrn = logged-in user, enforced in the serving layer, not just the table grant

Choosing the right mechanism#

I was confused at first. Row filter, column mask and serving view seemed to compete. They do not. They answer different questions, and a mature design layers them.

Mechanism The question it answers Where I used it
Object grant "May I query this at all?" Executives get Gold only. Billing gets claims only.
Row filter "Which rows may I see?" Department Gold metrics; department Silver tables
Column mask "I may see the row, but what value do I see in this column?" patient_mrn on Silver claims
Serving view "What may this consumer query, and how is it constrained?" security.patient_360_secure

Identity: three questions, three places#

A logged-in user is described in three separate pieces:

Groups I created#

I made six account-level groups: medcare_clinicians, medcare_department_admins, medcare_billing, medcare_executives, medcare_data_engineers and medcare_patients.

  • Consumer access ON gives the simplified environment for shared dashboards, Genie and Apps. It fits the business-facing roles.
  • Databricks SQL ON lets users work with SQL objects and dashboards.
  • Workspace access ON is for people who need the full workspace. In my demo that is clinicians and data engineers.
  • Admin access OFF for all six. A data engineer is not a workspace admin. I show data-engineer access through Unity Catalog privileges.

The spec's example names one group per department (cardiology_clinicians). I used one medcare_clinicians group and put the department in a map table. The map is the same idea with fewer groups.

My test identities: 2 clinicians (Cardiology, Neurology), 1 department admin (Cardiology), 1 billing user, 1 executive, 1 data engineer, 2 patients (MRN A and MRN B). The workspace admin identity stayed untouched.

The security schema#

security holds user_department_map ("which department may this user see?") and patient_identity_map ("which MRN belongs to this user?"). It also holds the filter and mask functions, patient_360_secure and access_review_log.

Before I inserted users, I read the exact department values from Silver. That avoids a filter failing over Cardiology vs cardiology.

The department row filter#

is_account_group_member() checks the role. session_user() identifies the person. The function checks the map table for the department.

  • Data engineers see all departments.
  • Executives see all departments, when the filter is used on Gold.
  • Clinicians and department admins see only their mapped department.
  • Everyone else sees no rows.

This function does not grant access. Grants are a separate layer. The function only decides which rows are visible after the user already has permission on the object.

I did not put medcare_billing or medcare_patients in this function. They should get no department-level clinical access at all.

I tested per user, not per group. The Cardiology clinician saw only Cardiology rows. The Neurology clinician saw only Neurology rows. A check on readmission_metrics for department <> 'Cardiology' returned 0 rows for the Cardiology clinician.

Where I attached it.

  • Gold: readmission_metrics, length_of_stay_metrics, lab_result_metrics, appointment_metrics, department_visit_metrics.
  • Silver, for clinicians: lab_results, patient_vitals, hospital_admissions, case, appointment. These have a department column.
  • Not silver.claim. Billing has its own access model.
  • Not silver.account. It has facility_id but no department. The spec gives clinicians patient_360 for their patients, not raw Account records. I did not invent a department filter for tables that have no department.

The patient filter and the serving view#

I built a patient filter function that checks patient_identity_map and tested it: Patient A saw their own MRN and not Patient B's, and the reverse. Then I decided not to attach it to patient_360.

Why? patient_360 serves several kinds of users with different rules. My first experiments put filters that read mapping tables onto the Gold table itself. I hit nested row and column policy errors. The Databricks docs say a filter or mask cannot reference a table that has its own active filter or mask. I dropped those experiments.

I split the concerns instead. gold.patient_360 stays the clean canonical table, with no patient filter. security.patient_360_secure is the controlled interface. This is the same idea as a dynamic view. The docs recommend not granting users read access to the tables behind such a view.

Grants: medcare_clinicians, medcare_patients and medcare_data_engineers get SELECT on the view. Nobody except the engineers gets SELECT on gold.patient_360.

Test results:

Test Result
Clinician A on patient_360_secure 133 Cardiology patients only
Patient A on patient_360_secure 1 patient: MRN000001
Patient A asks for MRN000002 0 rows
＋Added note · what 'their patients' meansAdded

The spec says clinicians get full patient_360 "for their patients". My view matches on department: a clinician sees patients whose latest known department is theirs. That is an approximation. A clinician who sees every patient in a department is not the same as a clinician with a care relationship to that patient. I would need a care-team mapping to enforce the second one. The spec does not define it.

Billing: a column mask#

The billing role needs claims and patient_mrn but no labs, vitals or clinical notes. Billing never receives the clinical tables. Then, inside Claim, the MRN column is masked for roles that should not see it.

Billing, clinicians and data engineers see the real MRN. Other roles see MASKED.

I defined the mask inside the Silver claim CREATE OR REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW, not with a later ALTER. A pipeline-managed materialized view can overwrite an ALTER-only change on the next update. The Databricks docs say materialized views accept ROW FILTER and MASK at creation. Billing gets silver.claim and gold.claims_metrics. I tested that Billing sees real MRNs and cannot read clinical data.

Executive and Data Engineer#

Executive. Dataset-level access, no row filters. The role needs all departments, so there is nothing to filter. I granted the Gold schema and seven aggregate Gold datasets. No patient_360, no Silver, no Bronze. This is a least-privilege grant design.

Data Engineer. Group-level access, never individual grants. The group got catalog access and all three layers, plus access to the department mapping. One member. I checked the engineer could work across layers:

Layer What the engineer saw
Bronze 15,075 lab rows
Silver 14,950 lab rows
Gold 1,001 patient_360 rows

I also checked that the engineer could see several departments.

Governance, audit and encryption#

  • Monthly review. I created security.access_review_log and recorded a review of the Data Engineer group (one member). It is a simple, auditable record that membership is reviewed monthly.
  • Audit logging. I did not build my own audit system. Unity Catalog already writes events to system.access.audit. I queried it and got records with user_identity.email, service_name = unityCatalog, action_name and a status code of 200.
  • Encryption. My platform ran on Databricks-managed infrastructure, where standard platform traffic uses encrypted channels. I did not set up customer-managed keys or worker-to-worker encryption. Those controls are not available in Databricks Free Edition. I did not tick an "encryption configured" box I could not verify.
＋Added context · encryption docsAdded

The Databricks encryption page says customer-managed keys are an Enterprise-tier feature. It also says traffic between worker nodes is not encrypted unless you add an init script that enables AES-128 inside a TLS 1.3 connection. That matches what I recorded. This is current documentation, not part of my spec.

Security gotchas I hit#

  • A successful pipeline can still show 0 rows. Silver Appointment showed 0 rows even though Bronze had 300. The transformation was fine. Row filters were hiding the rows from the wrong user. Pipeline success and Unity Catalog visibility are different things.
  • The identity that refreshes a materialized view matters. patient_360 first had many null clinical fields. The refresh ran under a security context that could not see the filtered Silver data. Test with the engineer identity to confirm.
  • Filters on mapping tables caused policy errors. I discarded those experiments.
  • USE SCHEMA is not data access. It is a prerequisite for using objects in the schema. It does not grant the objects themselves.

10AI Search and RAG

Spec · Vector Search + LLM Q&A Build · Steps 14–16 Notes · §7, §26–31

The spec asks for a Mosaic AI Vector Search index directly on the Gold tables patient_360, appointment_metrics and claims_metrics, plus Case descriptions, with no intermediate storage. Then I select that index in the Databricks Playground, attach it to an LLM, and test patient-style and admin-style questions.

⚠Patient-level retrieval needs identity controlsImportant

Authorization has to happen at retrieval time, from a verified identity. A system prompt that tells the model "only answer for this patient" is not access control. The model can be tricked, and the search index does not know who is asking.

AI Search does not support row and column permissions from the source table. The docs suggest application-level ACLs through the filter API. So I never call patient-level search safe on the index alone. The safe path is: authenticated user → authorized MRN lookup → mandatory filter → retrieval → LLM. I explain where my own build is weaker than that below.

Naming. The spec says "Mosaic AI Vector Search". My build notes say "AI Search". The current Databricks docs call it Databricks AI Search (formerly Databricks Vector Search). I use "AI Search" for the product and keep "Vector Search" when I quote the spec.

What I built#

  • An AI Search endpoint named medcare_ai_search and a dedicated schema healthcare_insights.ai_search.
  • Serving Delta tables, one per index. The Gold materialized views stay untouched. These tables exist only to feed AI Search.
  • For each serving table: one consolidated search_text column for embeddings. I did not want AI Search embedding 30 unrelated columns on their own.
  • patient_mrn stays a separate indexed field so I can filter on it, for example patient_mrn = MRN000001.
  • Change data feed enabled on each source table. A Delta Sync index on a standard endpoint needs it.
Index Indexed rows What it holds Filter verified
patient_360_index 1,000 patients Consolidated patient record patient_mrn
appointment_metrics_index 300 metrics Appointment metric rows department
claims_metrics_index 231 metrics 300 source claims aggregated by facility + payer + month Query verified
case_descriptions_index 300 cases case_id as primary key; MRN, facility, department, type, status, priority, description, timestamps, resolution hours patient_mrn

All four are HYBRID + DELTA_SYNC + TRIGGERED. All four use the same endpoint and embed search_text. A hybrid query combines vector similarity with keyword scoring.

Small details that bit me.

  • One patient had a null MRN. That explains 1,001 in Gold and 1,000 in the index. I did not invent an MRN for that patient, because it could attach their data to someone else. I removed the row only from the AI Search copy. Gold stayed intact.
  • The Case index first failed because resolution_time_hours had a DECIMAL type the index setup did not support. I changed the serving copy to DOUBLE, enabled the change feed again and the index was created.
  • An index sync once failed because the pipeline was still running. I waited, then the index reached ONLINE_NO_PENDING_UPDATE.

Retrieval and grounding flow#

Which index answers which question#

Question type Right source
Latest HbA1c patient_360 and/or Silver lab data
Next appointment patient_360
Latest claim approval patient_360
Doctor note / case case_descriptions
Appointment performance appointment_metrics
Claim turnaround by payer claims_metrics

Patient path in my build#

I wrote reusable retrieval functions and a build_rag_context() function. The patient branch cannot run without an MRN. I kept the four indexes separate because their data means different things.

My first combined test asked for the last HbA1c plus a doctor note. The filter worked. Retrieval was not enough: latest_lab_results was None, and the case index returned an appointment issue. I did not rush into the LLM. I also did not add a fifth index. I refreshed the existing 1,000-row patient serving table with a MERGE so it matched the corrected Gold values. That did not recreate the table or the index, and it did not touch Gold or Silver. The index then synced.

After that, for MRN000754:

  • The filter restricted retrieval to that MRN.
  • Patient 360 returned the real latest lab: HbA1c 4.33%, abnormal = false, at 2026-08-31 00:57.
  • The case index returned only that patient's case.

I sent that context to GPT-OSS 20B through ai_query. It answered: "Your most recent HbA1c result was 4.33% (from the lab taken on August 31, 2026)." A second function call for claim status gave "Approved on 2026-08-29".

This was the first version of the function. The caller supplies the MRN:

The patient filter inside retrieval looks like this. I show only the part I am sure of:

I then tested the claim question with MRN000002. The answer was "the information about your latest claim status isn't available". That MRN's claim fields were Unknown or null, so the model did not invent a status. That shows grounding. It does not show a security boundary. A caller who passed any MRN still got data back.

So I changed the function. The caller now passes the patient's email, and the function resolves the MRN from security.patient_identity_map:

Try it: where does the MRN come from?

How the filter value is set

    Even the “identity map” option depends on the identity being authenticated. In my tests the email was supplied by the caller. See the limits above.

    Admin path: AI Search is not an aggregation engine {#ai-admin}#

    For "Which department had the highest appointment no-show?", AI Search returned only the top 5 semantically similar rows. They were Emergency records from different dates and facilities, including one 100% no-show row. That does not prove Emergency is highest overall. I should not give that context to the LLM and let it guess.

    AI Search retrieves relevant rows. It does not calculate highest, lowest, count, average or trend. Those questions need an exact aggregation step on Gold.

    Seven Unity Catalog functions cover the Gold metrics:

    Topic Function
    Readmission fn_readmission_metrics
    Appointments and no-shows fn_appointment_metrics
    Claims fn_claims_metrics
    Length of stay fn_length_of_stay_metrics
    Labs fn_lab_result_metrics
    Department activity fn_department_visit_metrics
    Patient queries fn_patient_query_metrics

    The first exact function reproduced the validated result: Nephrology: 18.42% no-show rate (7 of 38 appointments).

    The agent and its deployment#

    My agent is not simply "question → LLM → answer". The LLM understands the intent and chooses a tool. The tool returns verified data. The LLM turns that into an answer. I had two main tools, patient_tool and admin_tool.

    Steps I took: I copied only six functions into the agent file (retrieve_patient_context, retrieve_admin_context, build_rag_context, validate_admin_sql, ask_patient, ask_admin), wrapped them as tools, tested the agent, registered it, fixed streaming and queried the deployed agent. I also built simple chat widgets for patient and admin with ipywidgets, as front ends for the functions.

    For final Playground testing I used an LLM endpoint along with the vector indexes and Unity Catalog functions, plus a system prompt. The agent states its limit plainly: "The agent can report department-level admission and appointment volumes. Unique patient counts are only reported where an explicit unique-patient metric is available."

    Databricks documents ResponsesAgent as the recommended interface for production agents. It requires a predict method, and for streaming it expects delta events followed by a final completion event. Unity Catalog functions can be agent tools.

    Limits of my build {#ai-limits}#

    ⚠Where my build is weaker than the rule at the topImportant

    I list these because they are real. They are my own analysis of my build, not statements from the spec.

    1. The identity came from the caller. The final patient function takes an email and maps it to an MRN. In notebook and Playground tests, I supplied the test email myself, and in Playground I wrote it into the system prompt. A string typed by the user, or written in a prompt, is not an authenticated identity. A real deployment needs the identity from the authenticated session, such as the signed-in user's token or an application layer that sets it. The model must never decide it.
    2. The index copy holds all patients. The patient index has 1,000 patients. AI Search ignores source-table permissions. Anyone who can query the index without a filter can read every row. I would restrict the index and endpoint with Unity Catalog privileges, and call it only from a service that adds the filter.
    3. Enforcement lives in application code. The filter is only as strong as the function that adds it. If another caller reaches the index directly, the filter is skipped.
    4. My notes record no adversarial testing. I tested two synthetic patients and one cross-patient request. I have no record of trying prompt injection or tampered identities.

    11Test questions I preserved

    Spec · Patient-style and admin-style questions Build · Steps 15, 16, 17

    The spec lists nine test questions. For each one I note the route, what my notes record and what to watch. Where my notes record no result, I say so.

    What was my last HbA1c result?

    Route: patient_360_index, latest lab results, filtered by the patient's MRN.

    What I recorded: For MRN000754 the context held HbA1c 4.33%, abnormal = false, collected at 2026-08-31 00:57. GPT-OSS 20B answered "Your most recent HbA1c result was 4.33% (from the lab taken on August 31, 2026)."

    Watch: My first test returned latest_lab_results = None. I had to refresh the serving copy before the answer worked.

    When is my next appointment?

    Route: patient_360.

    What I recorded: In my first combined test, the retrieved row for MRN000001 had no appointment populated. Gold initially showed 0 patients with appointments, which I treated as a legitimate result after checking the data. The model must not fill the gap. My notes do not record a successful next-appointment answer.

    Has my latest claim been approved?

    Route: patient_360.

    What I recorded: The function answered "Approved on 2026-08-29" for the tested patient. For MRN000002, claim fields were Unknown or null, and the model said the status was not available.

    What did the doctor note during my last visit?

    Route: case_descriptions_index with the patient MRN filter.

    What I recorded: The Case index returned only the patient's own case. In my first combined test it returned an appointment issue, not a clinical note.

    Watch: Case holds complaints and support cases, per the spec. None of the eight sources is a clinical-notes dataset. This question can only be answered if case descriptions contain the note. I would confirm what the data actually holds.

    Is my creatinine level improving?

    Route: patient_360 and/or Silver lab data.

    What I recorded: My notes record no test of this question.

    Watch (added note): A trend needs several creatinine results over time. patient_360 holds latest lab results. So the Gold row alone cannot show a trend. I would need a retrieval path to Silver lab_results. That is a design decision, and the spec does not make it.

    Which department had the highest readmission rate last month?

    Route: fn_readmission_metrics on readmission_metrics. It is not one of the four AI Search indexes.

    What I recorded: The generalized admin flow worked for readmission. I added routing rules after the agent once used fn_department_visit_metrics for this question. I added a rule for relative dates such as "last month", and a rule against inventing a year.

    How many patients visited Cardiology this week?

    Route: fn_department_visit_metrics, week grain.

    What I recorded: The first run returned Unknown, which led me to fix empty-result handling. The agent had also treated admission_count as a patient count. The final rule: admissions and appointments are not unique patients. If no distinct-patient metric exists, the agent says the unique count is not available.

    What is the average claim turnaround time by payer?

    Route: fn_claims_metrics.

    What I recorded: This worked. Claim averages need care: I use claim counts as weights, and I do not average monthly averages. In the Billing dashboard test, Average Claim Turnaround showed 9.0 days.

    Which department has the highest appointment no-show rate?

    Route: fn_appointment_metrics, with an exact aggregation.

    What I recorded: Nephrology at 18.42% (7 of 38 appointments). The top semantic hit had been a single Emergency row at 100%. That row was one day, not the department's overall rate.

    14Debugging log

    Build · Complete Debugging List

    I kept the full list because the bugs taught me more than the happy path. Use the search box to find a topic. The groups are collapsed.

    1 · S3 → Databricks setup
    • I was confused about using simulated storage instead of the real S3 source. Fix: use the real Amazon S3 bucket and actual CSV files.
    • S3 ingestion needed the right Bronze architecture. Fix: a Lakeflow pipeline with the four required CSV sources.
    2 · Salesforce ingestion
    • Salesforce objects had to be connected. Fix: a Lakeflow Connect connection importing Account, Case, Appointment and Claim.
    • S3 and Salesforce ingestion had to coexist in Bronze. Fix: keep them separate and preserve source metadata.
    3 · Silver-layer problems
    • Silver Appointment showed 0 rows while Bronze had 300. The transformation worked. The problem was the security filtering applied later.
    • Silver clinical tables looked empty with the wrong user or security context. Row filters changed what the querying user could see.
    • The pipeline showed success but the user still saw 0 rows. Pipeline execution and Unity Catalog access are different.
    • The diagnosis lookup was not fully implemented. Blank diagnoses became Unknown. The external lookup stays a known gap.
    • Account information needed masking and tokenization. Fix: masking and tokenization on sensitive Account fields.
    • Claim MRNs needed more protection. Fix: MRN masking on Silver claims.
    • Several Silver tables needed department restrictions. Fix: department row filters on the applicable clinical tables.
    4 · Gold-layer problems
    • patient_360 first had many null clinical fields. The materialized view refresh ran under a security context that could not see the filtered Silver data.
    • patient_360 had 1,001 rows but only 1,000 identifiable patients. I removed the null-MRN row from the AI Search serving copy only.
    • Gold had 0 patients with appointments. I checked the data and treated it as a legitimate result instead of rebuilding the pipeline again and again.
    • Gold metrics are event or metric rows, not necessarily unique patients. This mattered later in agent testing.
    5 · Security implementation problems
    • Department row filters first made clinical users see no data. Testing with the Data Engineer identity showed the security-context issue.
    • The Gold patient_360 materialized view could not just take the patient-level row filter. Several experiments caused nested policy errors.
    • Row filters on mapping or security tables caused policy problems. I discarded those experiments.
    • Patient access had to differ from clinician and admin access. Fix: patient_360_secure instead of exposing Gold patient_360.
    • I had to prove one patient could not retrieve another's record. I tested MRN000001 vs MRN000002.
    • Billing data needed separate protection. Fix: MRN masking and billing-specific access.
    • Audit logging first needed the right audit field. I found the status-code field that worked in my workspace.
    • Free Edition limits had to be respected. Customer-managed keys were not available, and I did not claim features I had not verified.
    6 · AI Search problems
    • AI Search first indexed the wrong or old patient_360 state. Fix: refresh the serving data with a MERGE rather than recreating Gold.
    • The patient index held stale data. After the serving table was corrected, the index synced.
    • An index sync failed because the pipeline was still running. I waited; the index became ONLINE_NO_PENDING_UPDATE.
    • AI Search needed patient-level filtering. I tested MRN000001 and MRN000002 and got one row per patient.
    • The Case index failed because resolution_time_hours had an unsupported DECIMAL type. Fix: DOUBLE in the serving copy, change feed enabled again.
    • AI Search could fetch individual metric rows but could not do reliable admin aggregation. This was the biggest issue in Playground testing.
    7 · Python and agent development
    • The normal OpenAI client expected OPENAI_API_KEY. Fix: use DatabricksOpenAI.
    • ResponsesAgent was used incorrectly. Fix: a proper subclass with predict().
    • I used the wrong model endpoint name. gpt-oss-20b gave ENDPOINT_NOT_FOUND. Fix: databricks-gpt-oss-20b for the Databricks OpenAI client.
    • I tested ResponsesAgent with .invoke(). Fix: use predict().
    • The generated Python file had leftover packaging and wrapper code. Fix: remove the old Path.write_text() section.
    • An unterminated triple-quoted string appeared after the wrapper was partly removed. Fix: clean the start and end of the wrapper.
    • The imported module had no agent. Fix: agent = MedCareAgent().
    • The test looked for the file in /mnt/data but the real Workspace file was elsewhere. Fix: correct the path.
    8 · MLflow
    • First model logging failed because I logged as code without mlflow.models.set_model(). Fix: set_model(agent).
    • The agent had to be registered in Unity Catalog. Fix: healthcare_insights.ai_search.medcare_agent.
    • Many model versions piled up while debugging. Fix: identify and deploy the corrected version instead of creating random versions.
    • The first Playground response was rejected because the assistant output lacked status: "completed". Fix: create explicit completed response output items.
    9 · Model Serving and SQL execution
    • Model Serving failed because the deployed agent tried to create a Spark session (Cluster id or serverless are required but were not specified). Fix: remove the Spark / Databricks Connect dependency from the runtime path.
    • I tried SQL Warehouse execution from the deployed agent. I first used the workspace ID instead of the warehouse ID by mistake.
    • Notebook SQL worked, but the deployed endpoint still had SQL problems. I tested the warehouse alone with SELECT 1.
    • ai_query() worked on its own.
    • The deployed runtime later gave Remote session creation failed: INTERNAL: An unknown error occurred. Notebook SQL success does not guarantee the same behavior inside Model Serving.
    • Architecture change: from direct SQL warehouse execution to Unity Catalog functions for admin analytics.
    10 · Streaming
    • AI Playground sent a streaming request and the endpoint failed with Streaming implementation not provided.
    • The agent had only predict(). Fix: add predict_stream() with ResponsesAgentStreamEvent.
    • I verified the event format against the current ResponsesAgent API and added the streaming wrapper.
    11 · Admin agent in Playground
    • The agent used AI Search for admin aggregate questions and got single rows instead of a department rate. Fix: explicit aggregation rules.
    • It treated a single 100% row as the department's overall rate.
    • It used fn_department_visit_metrics for readmission questions. Fix: strict function-routing rules.
    • Metric functions returned several grains (Day, Week, Month, Year). Fix: never combine them.
    • It could pick the highest single percentage instead of the department-level aggregate. Fix: weighted aggregation rules.
    • It treated admissions and appointments as patients ("How many patients visited Cardiology?" used admission_count). Fix: they are not unique patient counts.
    • That produced a plausible but wrong patient count. Fix: a hard rule to say unique patient count is unavailable when the metric lacks it.
    • Claims averages needed careful aggregation. Fix: use claim counts as weights, not averages of averages.
    • Relative dates ("this year", "this month", "last month", "this week") needed period-resolution rules.
    • The agent could invent a year when the user gave none. Fix: a rule against inventing dates or years.
    12 · Playground identity
    • Playground did not expose a visible user email. For the controlled test, I wrote the test email into the system prompt.
    • The patient email had to resolve to the authorized MRN rather than letting the user type any MRN. I kept that rule in the prompt and in the agent.
    Nothing matches that filter.

    The biggest lessons#

    1. Data ingestion: S3 and Salesforce both had to be connected correctly.
    2. Security context: pipelines worked, but users sometimes saw 0 rows because of Unity Catalog row filters.
    3. Gold refresh: patient_360 had null clinical data because of the execution identity.
    4. AI Search sync: serving data and indexes had to be refreshed correctly.
    5. Index schema compatibility: the Case index failed on a DECIMAL field.
    6. Agent API: wrong client, wrong model name, wrong ResponsesAgent use.
    7. MLflow packaging: missing set_model() and an invalid response status.
    8. Model Serving runtime: Spark and SQL warehouse session problems.
    9. Streaming: Playground required predict_stream().
    10. Analytics correctness: AI Search was not an aggregation engine, functions had different grains, and admissions were not unique patients.
    ★The lesson I want to remember most

    A system can return technically valid data and still give the wrong business answer. That happens when the agent misunderstands grain, aggregation or metric meaning.

    ＋Added context · why the SQL warehouse path may have failedAdded

    The Databricks docs say the function client runs tools on serverless general compute, and a SQL warehouse alone is not enough. That may be related to the remote-session errors I hit. I have not tested this.

    15SQL and AI cheat sheet

    Revision · Syntax & AI notes

    This is my revision list. Each row has the pattern and what it does in this project. Use the box to filter.

    Syntax What it does How I used it
    CREATE OR REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW Creates a materialized view and refreshes it if it exists. Databricks maintains the result. Silver and Gold tables
    SELECT … AS Choose columns; name or transform them. TRIM(UPPER(patient_mrn)) AS patient_mrn
    TRIM, UPPER, LOWER Remove spaces; change case. TRIM(UPPER(patient_mrn)) on the join key
    CAST Treat a value as another type. CAST(result_value AS DOUBLE), CAST(claim_amount AS DECIMAL(18,2))
    CASE WHEN SQL's if / elif / else. Status, type, category, channel, unit and vital-type cleanup
    IS NULL / IS NOT NULL Test for missing data. Never use = NULL. WHERE collected_datetime IS NOT NULL
    WHERE Keep rows that match a condition. WHERE rn = 1
    WITH (CTE) Named temporary step inside a query. standardized → validated → deduplicated
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (...) Numbers rows inside a group. Latest-record and deduplication pattern
    PARTITION BY Makes a separate group per key inside a window. Not physical partitioning. PARTITION BY patient_mrn
    ORDER BY … DESC Newest first. ORDER BY SystemModstamp DESC
    LEFT JOIN … ON Keep every left row; add matches from the right. Vitals keep their rows even without an admission
    DATE_TRUNC Truncate a timestamp to a unit. 'MINUTE' for sensor dedupe; 'MONTH' for metrics
    DATEDIFF(end, start) Difference in days. lead_time_days, turnaround_days
    UNIX_TIMESTAMP Seconds difference; divide by 3600 for hours. resolution_time_hours, length_of_stay_hours
    BETWEEN min <= value <= max. Lab range check
    REGEXP_EXTRACT(text, pattern, 1) Pull a piece of text with a regex. "12.0-17.5" → min 12.0, max 17.5
    MD5, SUBSTRING, ` `
    GROUP BY, COUNT, SUM, AVG Turn records into group-level metrics. Gold aggregates
    Conditional aggregation SUM(CASE WHEN condition THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) counts matches. No-shows, approved claims, abnormal labs, readmissions, cancellations
    NULLIF(denominator, 0) Avoids division by zero. 100.0 * numerator / NULLIF(denominator, 0)
    Metric grain The level a number represents. Do not add day + week + month + year rows. Agent aggregation rules
    AI Search Retrieves relevant information. Patient Q&A
    UC function Runs trusted, fixed analytics. Admin analytics
    LLM Reasoning and natural-language response. Writes the final answer
    Tool calling The LLM picks and uses tools. patient_tool, admin_tool
    ResponsesAgent Deployable MLflow agent with predict(). MedCareAgent
    set_model() Tells MLflow which object in the file is the agent. Logging the agent
    MLflow Packages and manages the model. log_model()
    Model Serving Exposes the agent as an endpoint. Playground queries it

    16Revision prompts

    Try to answer each one before I open it.

    What is the job of each medallion layer?

    Bronze keeps the source as-is plus metadata. Silver makes the data trustworthy. Gold makes business-ready metrics.

    Why is patient_mrn so important?

    It is the central join key between Salesforce patient data and clinical data. If it is inconsistent, patient_360, metrics and Q&A can all be wrong.

    Why did I not attach the patient filter to patient_360?

    patient_360 is the canonical Gold table and serves several user types. Filters that read mapping tables onto it caused nested policy errors. I kept Gold clean and put identity logic in patient_360_secure.

    Row filter, column mask, serving view: which question does each answer?

    Row filter: which rows may I see? Column mask: what value do I see in this column? Serving view: what may this consumer query, and how is it constrained?

    Does department_row_filter grant access?

    No. Grants decide whether a user can query the object. The filter only decides which rows they see after that.

    Why can a patient not just type their own MRN?

    Then they could type anyone's. The MRN must come from the authenticated identity through patient_identity_map, and the filter must be applied outside the model.

    Why is a prompt rule not access control?

    A prompt only asks the model to behave. The index does not enforce row permissions, and the model can be wrong or manipulated. Access control must be enforced before the data reaches the model.

    Why is AI Search wrong for a 'highest no-show rate' question?

    It returns the top semantic matches, not the full dataset. One row at 100% may be a single day. Aggregate questions need an exact calculation on Gold.

    Why must I never add day, week, month and year rows together?

    They describe the same events at different grains. Adding them double-counts.

    Are admission counts the number of patients?

    No. One patient can have many admissions and appointments. If there is no unique-patient metric, I say the count is not available.

    What does ROW_NUMBER() … WHERE rn = 1 give me?

    The newest record for each key, when I order by timestamp descending.

    Why did Silver Appointment show 0 rows when Bronze had 300?

    The transformation was fine. Row filters hid the rows from the querying user. Pipeline success and Unity Catalog visibility are different.

    Why does the billing mask live in the materialized view definition?

    A pipeline-managed materialized view can overwrite a change made later with ALTER.

    Nothing matches that filter.

    17Accuracy and version notes

    I keep this section separate on purpose. Everything here is added by me while checking my work. It is not part of the spec. I checked current Databricks documentation, and I note it where I did. I did not change anything above without flagging it here.

    # Type What I found What to do
    1 Version The spec says "Mosaic AI Vector Search". The current Databricks docs call it "Databricks AI Search (formerly Databricks Vector Search)". Many API paths still say vector-search. Use the current name in new notes; keep paths as they are.
    2 Version My notes name the audit result field response.status_code. The audit log reference shows statusCode in its example. My query returned records in my workspace. Check the real field names with DESCRIBE on system.access.audit.
    3 Deviation The spec says no intermediate storage. I built Delta serving tables for AI Search. The current docs list materialized views as supported index sources. Re-test an index directly on Gold. I have not tried.
    4 Deviation The spec says select the index in the Playground dropdown and attach it to an LLM. I ended with a custom agent, AI Search indexes and Unity Catalog functions, because the index alone could not do admin aggregation. Keep the reason in mind.
    5 Security The patient identity in my tests came from the caller or the system prompt. See the limits section. Use an authenticated identity.
    6 Security The AI Search index copy holds all 1,000 patients and ignores source permissions. Restrict index access with Unity Catalog and call it only through a filtering service.
    7 Security The spec asks for a column mask function on name, contact and address for every group except direct-care clinicians. I tokenized those columns in Silver for everyone. I only built a mask function for the claim MRN. Decide whether a group-based mask is still needed.
    8 Security MD5 of a name is a weak pseudonym. Use a salted or keyed method for real data.
    9 Security Regex redaction covers email, phone, MRN and DOB. It does not cover names. Review redacted samples before indexing.
    10 Spec gap "Their patients" for clinicians is approximated by department match. A care-team map would be needed for a true relationship.
    11 Spec gap "Doctor note" is routed to Case descriptions. Case holds complaints and support cases. No source in the spec holds clinical notes. Confirm what the descriptions contain.
    12 Spec gap "Is my creatinine improving?" needs a trend. patient_360 holds latest labs. Decide how to reach Silver labs safely.

    What the spec does not define#

    I keep this list so I do not pretend the document answers these:

    • exact row counts per source and the historical date range
    • the Salesforce environment and field API names beyond the objects and fields described
    • the facility list and the department and diagnosis lookup contents
    • the exact LLM model and the patient authentication mechanism
    • dashboard implementation details
    • the S3 ingestion mechanism and the incremental / CDC mechanism
    • how synthetic data is loaded into Salesforce
    • the exact syntax for every current Databricks feature

    18Glossary

    Term Meaning
    MRN Medical record number. My central patient join key.
    PHI / PII Protected health information / personally identifiable information.
    Medallion Bronze → Silver → Gold layering of data.
    Quarantine A separate table for rows that fail validation, like lab_results_quarantine.
    CTE Common table expression. A named step made with WITH.
    Materialized view A query whose result Databricks stores and keeps up to date.
    Auto Loader Incrementally reads new files from cloud storage.
    Lakeflow Connect Managed connector that ingests Salesforce objects.
    Row filter A function that hides rows a user should not see.
    Column mask A function that returns a masked value for a column.
    Serving view A view that gives a consumer a controlled, identity-aware slice.
    AI Search Databricks retrieval service over indexed data (formerly Vector Search).
    Hybrid search Vector similarity plus keyword matching.
    Delta Sync An index that follows a Delta source table.
    Change data feed Delta feature that records row-level changes; Delta Sync needs it.
    RAG Retrieval-augmented generation. Retrieve context, then let the LLM answer from it.
    Grounded answer An answer drawn only from the retrieved context.
    UC function A Unity Catalog function I can call as a trusted tool.
    Tool calling The LLM chooses and runs a tool, then uses the result.
    ResponsesAgent MLflow interface for deployable agents.
    Grain The level a metric represents: day, week, month or year.
    LOS Length of stay.
    30-day readmission An admission with a previous admission by the same patient inside 30 days.
